requirements.title: ANINT arguments have the required types and constant KIND
requirements.definition: A shall be of type real, and optional KIND shall be a scalar integer constant expression.

pending.kind-scalar-integer-constant: Future source-control plan only: compile a conforming call ANINT(2.5, KIND=KIND(0.0)) as the positive control; do not require a diagnostic for nonconstant KIND because this is an unnumbered Clause 16 program restriction.

requirements.title: ANINT result is real and follows KIND selection
requirements.definition: ANINT returns a real result; KIND selects the result kind when present and otherwise the result kind is that of A.

pending.result-real-type: Assign ANINT(2.25) to a real initialized to -777.0 and assert exact value 2.0; the declared real target and exact whole-number result avoid a default-state oracle.
pending.kind-present-selects-result-kind: Call ANINT(2.0, KIND=KIND(0.0)) and assert KIND(result)==KIND(0.0) plus exact value 2.0; KIND is present and the selected default real kind is portable.
pending.kind-absent-uses-a-kind: Call ANINT(2.0) without KIND and assert KIND(result)==KIND(2.0) plus exact value 2.0; the default real argument kind gives a portable absent-KIND oracle.

requirements.title: ANINT rounds to nearest whole number with ties away from zero
requirements.definition: ANINT returns the nearest integer value to A, and a halfway case chooses the integer with greater magnitude.

pending.nearest-positive: Use A = 2.0 + 1.0 / REAL(RADIX(1.0)**2), which is closer to 2 than to 3 for any permitted radix; initialize result to -777.0 and assert ANINT(A)==2.0 exactly. Also use B = 3.0 - 1.0 / REAL(RADIX(1.0)**2) and assert ANINT(B)==3.0 exactly.
pending.nearest-negative: Use A = -2.0 - 1.0 / REAL(RADIX(1.0)**2), which is closer to -2 than to -3 for any permitted radix; initialize result to 777.0 and assert ANINT(A)==-2.0 exactly. Also use B = -3.0 + 1.0 / REAL(RADIX(1.0)**2) and assert ANINT(B)==-3.0 exactly.
pending.tie-greater-magnitude-positive: Guard the tie case by first computing H = 0.5 and verifying 2.0 + H - 2.0 equals H and 2.0 + H is distinct from 2.0 and 3.0; only when that probe succeeds, initialize result to -777.0 and assert ANINT(2.0 + H)==3.0. If the probe fails, do not claim this tie facet for that processor.
pending.tie-greater-magnitude-negative: Guard the tie case by first computing H = 0.5 and verifying -2.0 - H + 2.0 equals -H and -2.0 - H is distinct from -2.0 and -3.0; only when that probe succeeds, initialize result to 777.0 and assert ANINT(-2.0 - H)==-3.0. If the probe fails, do not claim this tie facet for that processor.
